concerns.text: The aggregated-threshold schema forbids theta < 1.0, and research.md says 'schema-conformant records restricted to theta >= 1.0'. The sigmoid fit f(theta)=1/(1+exp[-a(theta-theta_c)]) is then fitted only on [1,3] — entirely at or above the theoretical transition theta_c=1. With no data in the low-probability regime below the transition, the sigmoid's left asymptote is unconstrained and theta_c estimates will be biased/unidentifiable. The sub-1.0 runs exist in raw records; the fit must use them (relax the schema minimum or fit from raw Parquet).

Fixed outlier cutoff 2.05 ignores finite-size edge fluctuations: Tracy-Widom fluctuations scale as N^(-2/3) (std ~0.037 at N=500, ~0.013 at N=1000). The finite-size phase sweeps N in {500,...,2000} where a fixed 2.05 tolerance yields materially different false-positive rates across N, confounding the finite-size comparison. Use an N-dependent cutoff (e.g. 2 + c·N^(-2/3)) or the recorded empirical bulk edge plus TW-scaled margin, at least for the finite-size analysis.

For the 'random-sparse' pattern with density p, the plan does not state how rank k and support density p are simultaneously realized — a random sparse support of density p generically gives full rank. Specify the construction (e.g. k spikes on a p-dense random support, with the residual spectral norm verified negligible) so that 'rank k' and 'density p' are genuinely independent structural variables as claimed in Statistical Rigor.
